content.value_statement: Unclear feature ideas are hard to turn into reviewable engineering work. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through requirements, design, and task breakdown using EARS notation.
actual_capabilities: Guides a three phase flow for requirements, design, and task breakdown.
Converts natural language feature requests into user stories.
Structures acceptance criteria with EARS notation.
Plans EPIC, Story, and Subtask specification documents.
Previews generated specification files and related branch or PR prompts.
limitations: It is a planning workflow, not an implementation engine.
It depends on user approval before moving between phases.
Branch and PR actions depend on separate `/branch` and `/pr` skills.
It does not validate generated files against a project schema.

use_cases.title: Clarify a New Feature
use_cases.description: Turn a rough feature request into user stories and acceptance criteria before implementation begins.

use_cases.title: Plan Engineering Work
use_cases.description: Break a large feature into EPIC, Story, and Subtask documents with dependencies and review points.

use_cases.title: Prepare Review Documents
use_cases.description: Create a specification package that can support branch creation and a later PR review.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic Spec
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a simple feature idea.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a spec for [feature]. Ask clarifying questions before drafting requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Refine Requirements
prompt_templates.scenario: Convert rough notes into structured requirements.
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn these rough requirements into user stories and EARS acceptance criteria: [requirements].

prompt_templates.title: Explore Design Options
prompt_templates.scenario: Add architecture context before tasks are created.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the existing codebase context for [feature]. Propose design options, tradeoffs, and a task breakdown.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Full Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a complete specification package for review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an EPIC, Story, and Subtask plan for [feature]. Include dependencies, file previews, and branch or PR approval prompts.

output_examples.input: Create a spec for OAuth login with multi-factor authentication.
output: A user story for secure login by end users and administrators.
Acceptance criteria for password login, OAuth linking, MFA challenge, and invalid credentials.
A proposed EPIC, Story, and Subtask structure for review.

output_examples.input: Break down reporting dashboard requirements for implementation planning.
output: An EPIC summary for dashboard reporting goals.
Stories for metrics ingestion, filtering, export, and access control.
Subtasks ordered by dependency with a preview of specification files.

best_practices: Provide target users, business goals, constraints, and known edge cases.
Review each phase before asking the assistant to continue.
Confirm repository side effects before branch or PR workflows run.
anti_patterns: Skipping design exploration when requirements are still unclear.
Using the skill to implement production code before the specification is approved.
Ignoring existing architecture when creating tasks and dependencies.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It guides requirements discovery, design exploration, and task breakdown for specification-driven development.

faq.question: Does it write production code?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on specifications, acceptance criteria, file plans, and review preparation.

faq.question: Can it create files?
faq.answer: The workflow previews specification files and asks for confirmation before generation.

faq.question: Does it use EARS notation?
faq.answer: Yes. It structures acceptance criteria with event, state, and condition based EARS patterns.

faq.question: Does it need other skills?
faq.answer: Branch and PR steps depend on separate `/branch` and `/pr` skills.

faq.question: Can teams use it outside Japanese projects?
faq.answer: Yes. The source instructions are Japanese, but the assistant can produce output in another requested language.
